name: Dispatch boundary
description: What the host refuses to dispatch, and how narrow a bound object can make its own reachable surface.

scenarios.title: A guest may ask whether a name is reachable
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service and a capability reference in guest hands
scenarios.when: guest code probes each for a method it defines
scenarios.then: both report that they respond to it

scenarios.title: Constructing a proxy is not acquiring a capability
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service
scenarios.when: guest code constructs an instance of the bound proxy
scenarios.then: that instance carries no dispatch of its own

scenarios.title: A capability reference cannot be constructed
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: guest code tries to construct a reference directly

scenarios.title: A reference the guest holds is frozen
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code asks the reference whether it is frozen

scenarios.title: Being frozen does not stop it working
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code dispatches through the frozen reference

scenarios.title: An object that only looks like a reference is refused
given: a Sandbox whose guest built an object carrying the reference's shape
scenarios.then: the guest refuses it before the host is asked

scenarios.title: The guest's own proxy refuses a reflective name
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service
scenarios.when: guest code calls a reflective name on the bound proxy

scenarios.title: A callable the host permitted still forwards
given: a Sandbox with a callable bound as a Service
scenarios.when: guest code calls it through the proxy

scenarios.title: A meta-programming name is refused, not dispatched
given: a dispatch naming a meta-programming method on a bound target
scenarios.then: it is refused rather than forwarded

scenarios.title: A reflective name is refused too
given: a dispatch naming a reflective method on a bound target
scenarios.then: it is refused rather than forwarded

scenarios.title: The permitted callable names still dispatch
given: a dispatch naming a permitted method on a callable target

scenarios.title: A Service's own method still dispatches
given: a dispatch naming a method the bound object defines itself

scenarios.title: Refusal is decided by who owns the method, not by its name
given: a bound object defining a method whose name matches a refused one

scenarios.title: A name nobody defines is refused as an undefined target
given: a dispatch naming a method the bound object does not define
scenarios.then: it answers as an undefined target

scenarios.title: A reflective object is refused as an answer, not referenced
given: a bound Service whose method answers a reflective gadget
scenarios.then: the answer is refused rather than given a reference

scenarios.title: A callable answer is still referenced
given: a bound Service whose method answers a callable
scenarios.then: the guest receives a capability reference

scenarios.title: An object may make itself unreachable by every name
given: a bound object whose narrowing predicate denies every name
scenarios.when: the guest calls any of its methods

scenarios.title: Narrowing follows the object through a reference
given: a narrowing object reached as a capability reference
scenarios.when: the guest calls a method it denies

scenarios.title: An object may permit exactly the names it chooses
given: a bound object whose narrowing predicate permits a subset
scenarios.when: the guest calls a permitted name and a denied one

scenarios.title: Narrowing cannot open what the boundary closed
given: a bound object whose narrowing predicate permits a reflective name

scenarios.title: A permitted name the object answers dynamically still runs
given: a bound object permitting a name it handles dynamically

scenarios.title: An object that narrows nothing keeps its whole surface
given: a bound object carrying no narrowing predicate
scenarios.then: they answer as an ordinary Service's would

scenarios.title: The narrowing predicate is not itself reachable
given: a bound object carrying a narrowing predicate
scenarios.when: the guest calls the predicate by name

scenarios.title: Both frontends refuse a reflective target the same way
given: a scenario calling a reflective name on a bound target
scenarios.then: they refuse it the same way

scenarios.title: A bare class used as a type tag is refused as an answer
given: a bound Service whose method answers a bare class or module
scenarios.then: the answer is refused rather than given a reference

scenarios.title: A class bound directly cannot be reached through its class-level surface
given: a class or module bound directly as a Service
scenarios.when: guest code calls one of its class-level methods
scenarios.then: the call is refused rather than forwarded

text: The host is the boundary. Every refusal here is witnessed where the host
decides it, and the guest-side mirror is witnessed separately as a
convenience rather than as the thing that holds — a guest that skipped its
own check would still be refused.
Refusal turns on who owns the method rather than on how it is spelled, so a
bound object defining a method whose name matches a refused one is answered
by its own. Without that scenario the rule would read as a list of forbidden
Narrowing sits beneath the boundary, never above it: an object may close its
surface as far as it likes and may not open what the boundary closed. Both
directions are witnessed, along with the predicate staying unreachable — a
narrowing an object could be asked to describe would be a surface of its own.
